meta.title: Self-hosting guide | Mault
meta.description: Run Mault with Docker Compose, Coolify, or directly on a Pi/Linux host. Prerequisites, installation and updates, step by step.

hero.title: Run Mault on your own server
hero.description: Run Mault on your own hardware. Pick your setup and the guide shows only the steps you need. Progress is saved in this browser.

setup.label: Your setup
setup.title: Choose your setup
setup.description: Your choices are saved in the URL, so you can bookmark or share this guide.

compose.title: Docker Compose
compose.description: Any server you manage. Builds the stack from the repo.

coolify.title: Coolify
coolify.description: Runs the prebuilt images from GitHub Container Registry.

pi.title: Pi/Linux
pi.description: Install directly with local Postgres, a USB webcam and a GPIO or external controller.

auth.label: Accounts and database

local.title: Built-in
local.description: Postgres and accounts run inside the stack. No outside services.

neon.title: Neon
neon.description: Hosted Postgres and Neon Auth. Adds email verification, password editing and social sign-in.

auth.piNote: The Pi/Linux installer sets up built-in accounts and local Postgres. Neon is available with Docker Compose or Coolify.

gpio.title: Pi controlled with GPIO pins
gpio.description: The Pi drives the PCA9685 and sensors directly over GPIO/I2C.

usb.title: ESP32 / Arduino
usb.description: An external controller connected to the host over USB or Bluetooth.

raspberry-pi.title: Raspberry Pi
raspberry-pi.description: Direct GPIO/I2C control on a Raspberry Pi.

orange-pi-zero4.title: Orange Pi Zero 4
orange-pi-zero4.description: Direct control with the Zero 4 GPIO/I2C hardware.

docker.text: Docker with Compose v2. This should print a version.

coolify.text: A Coolify instance with a server connected.

neonAccount.text: A Neon account. The free tier is enough.

node.text: Node.js, Git and pnpm on any machine, to run the Neon migrations. Corepack installs the right pnpm.

huggingface.text: Outbound access to huggingface.co for the scanner's model. Allowlist it in DNS blockers such as Pi-hole.

domain.text: Optional: a domain and an HTTPS reverse proxy for access outside your network.

piSystem.text: Use a Debian/Ubuntu-based Linux system with apt, systemd user services and available Postgres/pgvector packages, such as Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit). Install over SSH as a normal user with sudo access.

piHardware.text: Connect a USB webcam to the host and have your sorter ready: GPIO/I2C wiring for direct control, or an Arduino/ESP32 with compatible Mault firmware for USB or Bluetooth. Bluetooth also needs a BLE adapter on the host. Allow disk space for dependencies, builds and card data, and internet access for downloads.

piTools.text: Install Git and Python 3 before cloning. The installer prepares the remaining dependencies.

configure.label: Configure
configure.title: Configure
configure.description: All settings live in one .env file in the repository root.

secrets.text: Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER, IMPERSONATION_SECRET and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET, each to its own random value.
secrets.note: Run the command once per secret.

secretsNeon.text: Set IMPERSONATION_SECRET and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET, each to its own random value.

webUrl.text: Set WEB_URL to the address people will open, without a trailing slash. Keep http://localhost:8080 for a single machine.

webUrlNeon.text: Set WEB_URL to the address people will open, without a trailing slash. The Neon example points at the dev server, so change it, for example to http://localhost:8080.

userAgent.text: Set CARD_API_USER_AGENT to a name unique to your install, such as MyMault/1.0. Sources block names that overuse them.

start.label: Start
start.title: Start the stack
start.description: Compose builds the images and starts every service.

up.text: Build and start in the background.

logs.text: Watch the server start. It runs the database migrations itself.

logsNeon.text: Watch the server start. It connects to your migrated Neon database.

ports.text: Web app :8080, API docs :8081, API :3001. Postgres listens only on 127.0.0.1:5433.

portsNeon.text: Web app :8080, API docs :8081, API :3001. The bundled Postgres starts but isn't used.

firstRun.label: First sign-in
firstRun.title: Create your account
firstRun.description: Sign up, then add a game to match scans against.

signUp.text: Open your WEB_URL and sign up. The first account becomes platform admin with a Home organization.
signUp.note: Email verification, password editing, multi-session management and social sign-in need Neon.

signUpNeon.text: Open your WEB_URL, sign up and create your organization.

adminNeon.text: Make yourself platform admin in Neon's SQL editor.

game.text: Open /app/admin and sync your game’s card catalog first. Wait for vectorization to finish, then add the game in Games Manager and choose its fields using a synced sample card. Complete these steps before scanning.

admins.text: Optional: make another user platform admin. There's no screen for it yet.

prices.label: Prices
prices.title: Schedule price sync
prices.description: Prices come from TCGplayer, Cardmarket and Card Kingdom. Sync once a day, never more often: sources block installs that poll harder.

cron.text: Add this with crontab -e, replacing /opt/mault with your docker-compose.yml folder.
cron.note: Failed runs aren't retried. The next daily run catches up.

firstPull.text: After your first game sync, run the command once by hand. Cards have no price until then. Logs go to /var/log/mault-prices.log.

coolify.text: In Scheduled Tasks, add this command with container server and frequency 0 4 * * *.
coolify.note: After your first game sync, run it once from the server terminal. Failed runs aren't retried.

optional.label: Extras
optional.title: Optional features
optional.description: Each stays off until its variables are set. Restart or redeploy after changes.

discord.text: Discord bot: set DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and BOT_API_SECRET, then start with the bot profile.

discordCoolify.text: Discord bot: set DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and BOT_API_SECRET, then redeploy.

storage.text: File storage: point SCAN_IMAGE_BUCKET and the AWS_* variables at any S3-compatible bucket. Otherwise files are kept in Postgres.

email.text: Email: set RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM_EMAIL for password resets and invites. Otherwise invites are link-only.

wifi.text: Wi-Fi sorters: set SORTER_LINK_URL (or API_URL) to an address the sorter board can reach.

maintain.label: Maintenance
maintain.title: Updates and backups
maintain.description: Stay current and protect your data.

migrateNeon.text: Before each update, pull the latest code and run the Neon migrations.

update.text: Pull and rebuild. Migrations run on start-up.

updateCoolify.text: Redeploy. Coolify fetches the latest compose file and pulls the current image for your tag.

backupCoolify.text: Keep the mault-postgres volume across redeploys and back it up regularly.

backupNeon.text: Neon holds your data. Use its restore window and branches as backups.

secrets.text: Don't rotate secrets casually. A new OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER signs everyone out, and changing POSTGRES_PASSWORD doesn't update the existing database.

coolify.label: Coolify
coolify.title: Deploy with Coolify
coolify.description: Coolify runs the published images, so nothing builds on your server.

compose.text: Create + New > Public Repository with this URL, branch master, build pack Docker Compose and compose file /docker-compose-coolify.yml.

images.text: These images are pulled. Set MAULT_IMAGE_TAG (for example v1.2.3) to pin a version. The default is latest.

env.text: In the environment, set WEB_URL to your public origin without a trailing slash, and give POSTGRES_PASSWORD, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET each its own random value.
env.note: Leave VITE_API_URL and the Neon variables empty.

envNeon.text: In the environment, set these values, WEB_URL (no trailing slash) and your Neon values. Also give POSTGRES_PASSWORD, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, OWN_AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER and MONITOR_LINK_SECRET each its own random value, since the compose file requires them.
envNeon.note: Neon only accepts encrypted connections, hence DATABASE_SSL=true.

domain.text: Assign your domain to the web service on port 80, such as https://mault.example.com:80.

deploy.text: Deploy. The bot stays idle until its Discord variables are set.

neon.label: Neon
neon.title: Set up Neon
neon.description: Neon hosts the database, sign-in and file storage. The containers never migrate Neon, so you run the migrations yourself.

project.text: Create a project at console.neon.tech and run this in its SQL editor.

auth.text: Enable Neon Auth (Dashboard > Auth) before migrating.

urls.text: Copy the pooled connection string (DATABASE_URL), the auth URL (NEON_AUTH_URL and VITE_NEON_AUTH_URL) and the Data API URL (VITE_NEON_DATA_API_URL).

storage.text: Create a bucket in Neon's object storage and copy its name, S3 endpoint, region and keys into SCAN_IMAGE_BUCKET, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

clone.text: On a machine with Node.js, clone the repository, copy the Neon example config and set DATABASE_URL.

piHardware.label: Hardware
piHardware.title: Choose how the sorter connects
piHardware.description: Choose your controller and, for GPIO, your board above. The guide explains which options to choose when the installer prompts. Both modes use PI_HOST=1 and the host’s USB webcam.

gpio.text: Direct GPIO/I2C control uses PI_SORTER=1. The host controls the PCA9685 and sensors through the local Python controller. No Arduino/ESP32 firmware flashing is needed for this mode.

raspberry.text: Your selected board is Raspberry Pi (PI_SORTER_BOARD=raspberry-pi). The installer installs its GPIO/I2C dependencies and enables I2C.

orange.text: Your selected board is Orange Pi Zero 4 (PI_SORTER_BOARD=orange-pi-zero4). Use a supported Zero 4 system image with the libgpiod v2 Python API.
orange.note: Enable the image’s i2c0 boot overlay separately, then reboot so the header I2C adapter is available. Direct mode uses one built-in sorter.

usb.text: Your selected ESP32 / Arduino uses PI_SORTER=0. Connect a controller with compatible Mault firmware over USB or host Bluetooth. GPIO and I2C are not needed for external controllers.

bluetooth.text: For host Bluetooth, use a BLE-capable sorter and a host with a BLE adapter. The installer prepares BlueZ and the system Python Bleak package. Open Connect Bluetooth in the sorter menu, search for your sorter and select it.
bluetooth.note: The API owns the Bluetooth connection, so it works from remote browsers and during headless scans. Keep the sorter nearby and advertising, and disconnect other clients before connecting. Web Bluetooth instead uses the browser computer’s adapter.

piInstall.label: Installation
piInstall.title: Install Mault on the host
piInstall.description: Run these commands on the Pi or Linux host. The examples use ~/mault; choose a new directory for a fresh installation.

services.text: The installer installs the Node and pnpm versions pinned by the repository, Postgres with pgvector, ffmpeg and webcam tools. It creates the local database, builds Mault, runs migrations and enables user services at boot.
services.note: The web app listens on port 8080. The API, camera helper and link shortener listen on localhost and are reached through the web proxy. A controller service is added for GPIO mode.

settings.text: The installer saves your hardware choice and CARD_API_USER_AGENT in .env, along with local accounts, database credentials and secrets. Your chosen user-agent name identifies this installation’s card and price API requests. Reruns keep the saved name.
settings.note: Price sources use this name to identify requests. A blocked shared default name can affect other installs using it. A unique name does not remove request limits: schedule price sync only once a day.

installUsb.text: Run this command as your normal user, without sudo in front. Choose the external ESP32 / Arduino option when asked. Enter your sudo password when prompted, then type a unique name for the card and price API user agent, or press Enter to accept the generated name.
installUsb.note: Installation is headless by default. Reruns preserve the hardware choice and user-agent name already saved in .env.

installRaspberry.text: Run this command as your normal user, without sudo in front. Choose direct GPIO/I2C control, then Raspberry Pi when asked. Enter your sudo password when prompted, then type a unique name for the card and price API user agent, or press Enter to accept the generated name.
installRaspberry.note: Installation is headless by default. Reruns preserve the hardware choice and user-agent name already saved in .env. If the installer asks for a reboot to enable I2C, reboot and rerun the same command. Direct mode uses one built-in sorter.

installOrange.text: Run this command as your normal user, without sudo in front. Choose direct GPIO/I2C control, then Orange Pi Zero 4 when asked. Enter your sudo password when prompted, then type a unique name for the card and price API user agent, or press Enter to accept the generated name.
installOrange.note: Installation is headless by default. Reruns preserve the hardware choice and user-agent name already saved in .env.

piOpen.label: First use
piOpen.title: Open the app and prepare scanning
piOpen.description: Use a phone or computer on the same network. The host provides the camera and sorter connection.

address.text: Find the host’s LAN address, then open http://HOST_IP:8080 in your browser, replacing HOST_IP with that address. On the host itself, use http://localhost:8080.
address.note: Allow port 8080 on your LAN firewall if needed. Remote browsers reach the API through the web app; they do not need direct access to ports 3001 or 8765.

account.text: Sign up on your own installation. The first account becomes platform admin with a Home organization.

game.text: Open /app/admin and sync your game’s card catalog first. Wait for vectorization to finish, then add the game in Games Manager and choose its fields using a synced sample card. Complete these steps before scanning.
game.note: On a Pi host, “Start on this computer” uses your browser computer to vectorize missing card images. Keep the admin page open until it finishes. Live scans identify cards on the host.

scan.text: Open the scanner and calibrate your sorter. GPIO mode attaches the built-in sorter automatically; external-controller mode lets you connect the sorter over USB or host Bluetooth. The camera helper owns the USB webcam, so remote browsers do not need camera permission for it.

piPrices.label: Prices
piPrices.title: Schedule daily price sync
piPrices.description: The installer does not schedule price sync. After syncing your first game, pull prices once and set up a daily user timer for TCGplayer, Cardmarket and Card Kingdom.

firstPull.text: Run the price sync once after your first game sync. This loads the database connection and CARD_API_USER_AGENT from your .env file.
firstPull.note: Cards have no price until the first pull. Avoid repeated manual runs and use --force sparingly; price sources can block excessive requests.

schedule.text: Run this once as the user who installed Mault. It creates a user service and schedules price sync for 04:00 in the host’s time zone each day.
schedule.note: These paths assume ~/mault; change WorkingDirectory if you installed elsewhere. The host must be on at 04:00. Missed or failed runs wait for the next daily run; there are no automatic retries.

check.text: Check the next scheduled run and the price-sync log. The installer’s user linger setting lets the timer run after you disconnect from SSH.

piMaintain.label: Maintenance
piMaintain.title: Update and look after the host
piMaintain.description: Run maintenance from a terminal on the host, as the same user who installed Mault.

update.text: Finish scanning, disconnect the sorter and stop database syncs, then run the updater. It fetches the installed branch’s tracking branch, rebuilds, migrates the database and restarts services. Refresh your browsers when it finishes.
update.note: The updater stops if the checkout has changed or added files, or diverging commits. Preserve your work before retrying. If it fails after stopping services, fix the reported error and rerun it.

backup.text: Back up Postgres regularly. Enter POSTGRES_PASSWORD from .env when prompted. This writes the backup outside the checkout so it does not block updates.
backup.note: Also keep secure backups of .env and, in direct mode, .pi-controller/calibration.json. Do not change database passwords or account secrets casually.

logs.text: For startup or scan failures, inspect the API log.

automatic.text: Mault’s app services start automatically when the host powers on or reboots. The installer enables them at boot, so you normally do not need the manual start and stop commands below.

start.text: Manually start Mault when needed. From SSH it starts the services; in a graphical session it can also open Chromium if installed.

stop.text: When you need to stop Mault, finish any scan first and run this command.
